title: They imploded on day one. The world searched for 4 more days.

scenes.voiceover: A submersible went missing near the Titanic. For four days, the world watched a countdown clock. It turns out, they were already gone.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: dark ocean deep water submersible descending

scenes.voiceover: On June 18, 2023, the Titan submersible launched toward the Titanic with five people aboard. An hour and 45 minutes into the dive, it stopped checking in.
What followed was a four-day international search. Sonar picked up banging sounds. Officials estimated 96 hours of oxygen. The whole world was watching.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: coast guard ship search ocean aerial

scenes.voiceover: But officials later revealed a secret US Navy listening system had detected an implosion signature on day one. They had most likely died within hours — while the world spent four more days hoping.
And this wasn't bad luck. For five years, engineers and experts had warned the CEO, in writing, that the sub could kill someone. He ignored every one of them.
The full story of every warning OceanGate ignored is on the channel. Subscribe to mindwired.
